problem: Prior VLN tasks treat navigation in isolation or pair it with only one extra ability; no task interleaves outdoor navigation, object referring-expression comprehension, and egocentric assembly over multiple turns with cascading errors.
motivation: Real agents (e.g. warehouse robots) navigate to perform another task and repeat subtasks, so errors cascade across phases. The paper builds a joint navigation-assembly task and dataset to study this interweaving.
key_idea: Introduce ARRAMON, a Unity-based task where an agent follows NL instructions to navigate a city and collect target objects, then arranges them in an egocentric grid by NL spatial instructions, alternating for two turns.
insight: Metrics are coupled across phases: with perfect navigation (CTC-3=1.0) val-seen PTC is 0.382 versus 0.044 at the real CTC-3 of 0.098. Turn-2 scores are much lower than turn-1 (nDTW 0.049 vs 0.222), showing cascading errors. Vision-only, language-only and random-walk baselines all score far below vision+language, indicating the dataset is not modality-biased. The large human-model gap (nDTW 0.66 vs 0.135) shows the task is hard.
method: Task: two turns, each a navigation phase (find and pick up a target object in a city section) then an assembly phase (place it on a 4x5 grid relative to other objects); actions are forward, left/right 30°, and pickup/place.

Simulator/dataset: Unity simulator with a Mapbox-based city split into 7 sections; AMT Stage 1 workers write instructions along A* GT paths, and Stage 2 workers verify them (3 each; kept if nDTW>0.2 in both navigation turns and PTC=1 in both assembly turns). Result: 7,692 task instances (30,768 instructions), plus Hindi extension.

Metrics: nDTW, CTC-k (collected target correctness within distance k), rPOD = 1/(1+D^2) with Manhattan distance D, and PTC (placed target correctness). Assembly scores are 0 if the wrong object was collected.

Vision-and-Language baseline: ResNet visual features (7x7x2048), LSTM instruction encoder, bidirectional cross-attention (BiDAF-style) between vision and language, an action LSTM, attention over both fused features, and a linear layer giving action logits. Trained with teacher forcing and cross-entropy.
Ablation baselines: vision-only and language-only (no cross-attention), random walk, shortest path (A*), and human workers/expert.
Splits: sections 1-5 form train/val-seen (80/20), section 6 is val-unseen, section 7 is test-unseen.

setting.backbone: ResNet visual encoder + LSTM language encoder + bidirectional cross-attention, LSTM action decoder (trained from scratch, 1.83M trainable parameters)
setting.training_data: ARRAMON train split: 4,267 task instances (17,068 instructions/paths)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB view (ResNet features) plus natural language instruction
setting.simulator: custom Unity ARRAMON simulator (Mapbox city + assembly grid)
setting.privileged: none (at test time, if the agent fails to pick up or place, the closest object/location is used to let it proceed)

numbers.extra: assembly metrics computed assuming CTC-3 counts as a successful pickup

results: The V/L baseline reaches only nDTW 0.135/0.109/0.114 (val-seen/val-unseen/test-unseen) and PTC 0.044/0.028/0.035, with CTC-0 of 0. It beats the vision-only, language-only and random-walk baselines (e.g. val-seen nDTW 0.135 vs 0.110 language-only, 0.055 vision-only, 0.045 random). Human workers score nDTW ~0.67 and PTC ~0.86, so the human-model gap is large.
limitations: Baseline models are very weak (CTC-0 = 0), and evaluation relaxes the task by auto-proceeding with the closest object/location and using CTC-3 to compute assembly metrics.
The environment is synthetic, with a small set of object types, two patterns and seven colors, and only two turns. The dataset is modest in size with a single simulator and no real-robot evaluation.
Only simple baselines are provided; no stronger or pretrained models are explored. The Hindi extension is not evaluated.
